increment_paragraph: **RETURN-FAMILY-STAR-OUTSIDE-ROOT-PARENTHESES** (USER DECISION 2026-11-24: "launch the two return-family follow-up cards"; gateway rule 74s, extending rule 74m; `QCore.ReturnFamilyStarOutside`; [report](../../reports/return-family-star-outside-parentheses/README.md)). Family S of `legacy_return_family` admits a may-bind name only as the root of one dereference, but for a starred root `stars_before` stopped at a binary operator or at a `*` beyond the root's own parentheses, and `ends_one_dereference` read only up to those parentheses. `long w(long **q) { return *(*q + 1); }`, `*((long *)*q + 1)`, `*(1 + *q)`, `*(long *)(*q + 1)`, `(*q + 1)[0]` and `(*q + 1)->f` were therefore `Safe` at the base, while `return **q;` keeps the return refusal. The outer `*`, `[` or `->` dereferences a pointer computed from the value `*q` reads, a second dereference. A starred root is now refused when any parenthesised group enclosing it may be dereferenced: a `[` or `->` after its `)`, or a `*` before its `(` (read back through parenthesised groups) that is unary under either of rule 74h's readings. The reader cannot tell whether such a group's value derives from the root, so every one refuses. The admission is rule 74m's and that further condition, so the change only refuses (`the_fix_only_refuses_more`, `admitted_is_one_dereference`). `*q`, `(*q)`, `*q + 1`, `n * (*q + 1)` and `(T) *q` keep their admission and `*(T *)*q` rule 74m's refusal. After `k_free(q)`, `return *(*q + 1);` moves from `Unsafe` (`UseAfterRelease`) to the return refusal. Pinned at unit level (`tests/unit/legacy_return_family_star_outside.rs`, including `QCore.ReturnFamilyStarOutside.outsideVectors`) and end to end (`tests/return_family_star_outside_parentheses.rs`); every change pin fails at the base. Opt-in `current --monkey-linked` over Fluent Bit 046accf6: no row moves (1,171 / 2 / 3,623 / 8 on both sides), as predicted. The pinned system and slice routes need build/cycle19 inputs this host lacks and were not run. One adjacent gap is registered: RETURN-FAMILY-SUBSCRIPT-ENCLOSING-STARRED-ROOT.

ledger.why: Discharged by RETURN-FAMILY-STAR-OUTSIDE-ROOT-PARENTHESES (rule 74s). Reachability: `long w(long **q) { return *(*q + 1); }` and `return *((long *)*q + 1);` reached family S and were `Safe` at the base, as were `*(1 + *q)`, `*(n + *q)`, `*(*q - 1)`, `*(long *)(*q + 1)`, `(*q + 1)[0]` and `(*q + 1)->f`, while `return **q;` kept the return refusal (report §1). crates/qcore-c-gateway/src/legacy_return_family.rs adds `outside_dereference` and `group_dereferenced`: a starred may-bind root is refused when a parenthesised group enclosing it is followed by `[` or `->`, or is preceded (through parenthesised groups) by a `*` that rule 74h's `operator_at` reads as unary under either reading. Every such group refuses, because the reader cannot tell whether its value derives from the root. The admission is rule 74m's conjoined with that condition, so nothing admits more than at the base (`QCore.ReturnFamilyStarOutside.the_fix_only_refuses_more`, `admitted_is_one_dereference`). `*q`, `(*q)`, `*q + 1` and `(T) *q` keep their admission and `*(T *)*q` its refusal. `return *(*q + 1);` and `return *((long *)*q + 1);` are pinned as refused end to end (crates/qcore-c-gateway/tests/return_family_star_outside_parentheses.rs) and at unit level, and the change pins fail at the base. The opt-in corpus measurement shows no move, as predicted (report §5). The pinned system and slice routes need build/cycle19 inputs this host lacks and were not run.

ledger.title: Family S admits `n[*q]` with a scalar `n` and a may-bind `q` as one dereference
ledger.text: RETURN-FAMILY-STAR-OUTSIDE-ROOT-PARENTHESES found (report §6, by an end-to-end probe at its base and its tip) that crates/qcore-c-gateway/src/legacy_return_family.rs `scalar_read` admits a starred may-bind root inside a subscript's brackets: `long w(long **q, long n) { return n[*q]; }` is `Safe` at both. C11 6.5.2.1p2 makes `n[*q]` `*(n + *q)`, which rule 74s refuses; with a scalar `n` the pointer dereferenced is computed from the value `*q` reads, a second dereference. Rule 74s reads only parenthesised enclosing groups, so a bracket enclosing the root is not counted. With a pointer subscripted base (`a[*q]`, `a` untracked) the access is `a`'s, which is a base of the read node, so refusing every bracket would cost that admission. The direction is admitting. DISCHARGE: refuse a starred may-bind root inside a subscript whose subscripted operand is not known to be a pointer (a declared scalar, a number, an undecided name), keeping `a[*q]` for an untracked pointer `a` only where the reader can say `a` is the pointer, or show that no such return reaches family S. Pin `return n[*q];` end to end and measure.
